items.definition: to put a system, tool, or resource into effective use

examples.source: The team decided to deploy the new model gradually rather than release it to all users at once.
examples.translation: Das Team entschied sich, das neue Modell schrittweise einzuführen, anstatt es allen Nutzern auf einmal bereitzustellen.

examples.source: You can design elegant software in theory, but the real test begins when you deploy it in production.
examples.translation: Man kann elegante Software theoretisch entwerfen, aber der eigentliche Test beginnt, wenn man sie produktiv einsetzt.

examples.source: During the outage, engineers deployed a temporary fix while they investigated the deeper cause.
examples.translation: Während des Ausfalls spielten die Ingenieure eine vorläufige Lösung ein, während sie die eigentliche Ursache untersuchten.

items.definition: able to grow or handle increased demand without losing performance

examples.source: A clever prototype is not enough if the architecture is not scalable.
examples.translation: Ein cleverer Prototyp reicht nicht aus, wenn die Architektur nicht skalierbar ist.

examples.source: The investors were less interested in the demo than in whether the business model was scalable.
examples.translation: Die Investoren interessierten sich weniger für die Demo als dafür, ob das Geschäftsmodell skalierbar war.

examples.source: Cloud services can make a product more scalable, but they do not remove the need for good design.

items.definition: to convert information into a coded form so that unauthorised people cannot read it

examples.source: The policy requires staff to encrypt data before transferring files outside the organisation.
examples.translation: Die Richtlinie verlangt, dass Mitarbeitende Daten verschlüsseln, bevor sie Dateien außerhalb der Organisation übertragen.

examples.source: Even small firms should encrypt data on laptops that travel regularly.
examples.translation: Auch kleine Firmen sollten Daten auf Laptops verschlüsseln, die regelmäßig unterwegs sind.

examples.source: They discovered only after the incident that one legacy tool could not encrypt data properly.
examples.translation: Erst nach dem Vorfall stellten sie fest, dass ein Altsystem Daten nicht richtig verschlüsseln konnte.

items.definition: the ability of different systems or tools to work together effectively

examples.source: Without interoperability, hospitals end up duplicating information across incompatible systems.
examples.translation: Ohne Interoperabilität doppeln Krankenhäuser Informationen über inkompatible Systeme hinweg.

examples.source: The conference focused less on flashy innovation than on the boring but essential issue of interoperability.
examples.translation: Die Konferenz konzentrierte sich weniger auf auffällige Innovation als auf die langweilige, aber wesentliche Frage der Interoperabilität.

examples.source: Interoperability becomes critical the moment a product leaves the lab and enters a real ecosystem.
examples.translation: Interoperabilität wird in dem Moment kritisch, in dem ein Produkt das Labor verlässt und in ein reales Ökosystem eintritt.

items.definition: to stop using or providing something gradually rather than suddenly

examples.source: The company plans to phase out the old portal over six months.
examples.translation: Das Unternehmen plant, das alte Portal über sechs Monate schrittweise auslaufen zu lassen.

examples.source: Rather than forcing a dramatic switch, they phased out the legacy process in carefully managed stages.
examples.translation: Anstatt einen abrupten Wechsel zu erzwingen, ließen sie den Altprozess in sorgfältig gesteuerten Phasen auslaufen.

examples.source: A tool should be phased out only after users have a credible alternative.
examples.translation: Ein Werkzeug sollte erst dann auslaufen, wenn die Nutzer eine glaubwürdige Alternative haben.

examples.source: When systems interact, troubleshooting becomes as much about communication as about code.

examples.source: She documented each step carefully so the team could troubleshoot similar failures faster next time.
examples.translation: Sie dokumentierte jeden Schritt sorgfältig, damit das Team ähnliche Fehler beim nächsten Mal schneller beheben konnte.

examples.translation: Aus Sicht des Nutzers sollte sich der Zahlungsvorgang reibungslos anfühlen.

examples.source: The migration looked seamless on the outside, though it required months of careful preparation.

examples.source: A seamless interface is often the visible result of invisible engineering discipline.

pages.text: The company’s new analytics platform had impressed everyone in the demo, but the real pressure began when the team prepared to deploy it in production. The engineers knew that a flashy prototype meant little if the system was not scalable and if every regional unit had to invent its own workaround. During the planning session, one architect kept returning to interoperability: if the platform could not exchange information cleanly with existing tools, the promised efficiency gains would never arrive.

Security complicated the discussion, as it usually does. Customer files had to be handled in a way that allowed teams to collaborate without exposing the organisation to unnecessary risk. That meant they needed to encrypt data by default, not as an afterthought. It also meant recognising where legacy components were still vulnerable to attack. Some of those older tools used proprietary formats, which made integration slower and limited what the support team could do when incidents occurred.

In the end, the leadership group agreed to roll out the platform in controlled stages while they phased out the old reporting process. The support team built a clear runbook to troubleshoot failures quickly, and the product lead kept insisting that the user experience should feel seamless from the first login onward. The launch was not dramatic, but it was disciplined, and that is precisely why it worked.
